title: Lookup functions: XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, INDEX and MATCH

videos.script: Every sale in our sheet says CER1K. It never says what a bag of CER1K costs. {{code}} That answer lives in another sheet, on one row of the products table. A lookup is how a formula goes and gets it. {{lookup}} It takes three things. What to look for. Where to look. And what to bring back. {{three}} XLOOKUP asks for exactly those three, in that order. It is the one to write today. {{xlookup}} But most workbooks you open will use VLOOKUP. It counts columns by number. It guesses, unless you tell it not to. And it cannot look to its left. Each of those fails without an error. {{vlookup}} INDEX and MATCH do the same job in every version of Excel. MATCH finds the row. INDEX reads it. {{index}} Some lookups should not find the key at all. They should find the last threshold it passed. A sale of fourteen bags is large, because it passed ten. {{approximate}} And then the failures. A space you cannot see. A customer with no city, who comes back as zero. {{missing}} By the end, every sale will know its list price, its cost and its margin. {{margin}}
